page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by AWS Graviton processors built on the arm64 architecture. Operating on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor, the instance supplies 16 dedicated physical cores at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz, mapping directly to 16 vCPUs with one thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading. It is provisioned with 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 compute-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core.

The server integrates 950 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD instance storage, enabling high-throughput and low-latency disk operations directly on the physical host. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 8 Gbps. The configuration does not include discrete GPU acceleration, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

By coupling dedicated arm64 processor cores with bundled high-speed local NVMe storage, the c9gd.4xlarge provides strong resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require fast scratch space alongside CPU throughput. The hardware profile is appropriate for CI/CD compilation pipelines, batch compute tasks, video encoding, and distributed data transformation jobs that rely on fast temporary caching.
